@CairoScene #SceneAD: For the third consecutive year, ESLSCA University is returning to El Gouna Film Festival as its Official Educational Partner, with an expanded programme designed to bring those two worlds closer together.

For the festival’s ninth edition, the partnership places students from ESLSCA’s School of Visual Arts & Creative Industries inside the working ecosystem of one of the region’s major film gatherings, giving them access to filmmakers, industry professionals, and emerging talent.

This year, that access stretches across the school’s Cinematic Studies and New Media & Communication departments. Cinematic Studies students will receive full festival passes, while New Media & Communication students will cover their peers’ participation and relevant festival activity, turning El Gouna itself into a space for professional practice.

There will be two annual scholarships that will cover full tuition for three years for promising filmmakers from across Egypt’s governorates. Two students will receive full funding to participate in CineGouna Emerge. Students will also take part in Meet the Experts sessions with film professionals.

The Island in El Gouna will bring together students, faculty and members of the film community, showcasing selected projects by Cinematic Studies students. Elsewhere in the festival programme, an ESLSCA × Thndr workshop will explore entrepreneurship and financial independence alongside artistic practice.

ESLSCA will also announce Egypt’s first Master of Fine Arts in Filmmaking. The MFA will combine advanced filmmaking practice with postgraduate academic study, creating a specialised graduate pathway for filmmakers in Egypt.

The partnership was formalised through an MoU signed by Kareem ElHennawy, Secretary General and CEO of ESLSCA University, and Amr Mansi, CEO and Co-Founder of El Gouna Film Festival, in the presence of Hayat Aljowaily, Director of CineGouna Emerge & International Engagement, and Andrew Mohsen, Artistic Director of GFF.

@CairoScene #SceneAD: An MBA takes a few years. But creating an MBA programme that has the people who set the global benchmark saying, yes, this meets our standards, takes considerably longer. @eslscaeg, which just saw its flagship business degree awarded EFMD Programme Accreditation, that process has been years in the making.
 
It started with a dream to take the university’s MBA programme, which first launched in 1998 to bring global business education into conversation with the realities of working in Egypt, through EFMD Global’s accreditation process, a route that would put everything from its curriculum and teaching to its international exposure, corporate connections and quality assurance under a rather serious microscope. Over a decade later, the ESLSCA MBA has come out the other side with the accreditation. 
 
And it comes with a rather significant footnote: it is the first MBA programme in Egypt, the Middle East and Africa to receive it. 
 
That distinction matters because EFMD Programme Accreditation is not a participation trophy. The process evaluates everything from how a programme is designed and taught to how students are assessed, how closely it connects to industry and how seriously an institution takes the less glamorous but very important business of improving itself.
 
Of course, an accreditation like this does not belong to one dean, one faculty member or one graduating class. It is the accumulated work of the people who have taught the programme, run it, studied through it, graduated from it and, in many cases, gone on to carry the ESLSCA name into boardrooms and businesses of their own.
 
And while the accreditation marks a major milestone for the programme, it also gives the university a new benchmark to work from, rather than a reason to stop moving. Which means, now that ESLSCA has finally got the recognition it spent 14 years chasing, it has the slightly harder job of actually living up to it.

For the full feature head to scenenow.com or download the app - link in bio.

We are exhilarated to announce that the ESLSCA University MBA program has officially been awarded the prestigious EFMD Accredited label by EFMD Global!  
 
This milestone makes ESLSCA University home to the only EFMD-accredited MBA program in Egypt, the Middle East and Africa. 
 
This international seal of quality is a powerful testament to our community’s hard work, dedication, and shared vision for premium management education. Achieving our initial EFMD Programme Accreditation places ESLSCA among an elite tier of global institutions recognized for:  
 
Academic Excellence: High-quality curricula that meets rigorous global benchmarks.  
International Orientation: A truly global perspective integrated into our learning models.  
Corporate Relevance: Deep connections to real-world business practice and industry insights.  
Responsible Leadership: A core commitment to ethics, sustainability, and impactful management.  
 
We want to extend our deepest gratitude to our exceptional faculty, dedicated staff, ambitious students, successful alumni, and valued corporate partners. This milestone belongs to all of you.  
 
As we celebrate this breakthrough achievement, we remain steadfast in our mission to deliver transformative education that empowers the next generation of business leaders to shape a dynamic global economy.  
 
#ESLSCA #ESLSCAUniversity #EFMD #EFMDAccredited

First Day of MSc Classes!

A warm welcome to our MSc students as they begin their academic journey at ESLSCA University in collaboration with EDC!

Welcomed by Dr. Malek Ben Abdellatif, MSc Program Director, our students kicked off their first day of classes, marking the start of a journey filled with learning, growth, and new opportunities.

#ESLSCAUniversity #GettingYouFutureReady

Dr. Kareem ElHennawi, Secretary General & CEO of ESLSCA University, expressed his excitement about being part of El Gouna Film Festival during his speech at the “Reframing the Scene” event, highlighting ESLSCA’s commitment to building meaningful industry partnerships that enrich the student experience and create valuable opportunities for hands-on learning.

#ESLSCAUniversity #GettingYouFutureReady

Advancing the future of filmmaking education in Egypt!

Dr. Mervat Abou Oaf, Dean of ESLSCA University's School of Visual Arts & Creative Industries, shared her vision for advancing cinematic education, empowering the next generation of filmmakers, and bridging academic learning with industry experience during her speech at the “Reframing the Scene” event at El Gouna Film Festival, marking the launch of ESLSCA University's MFA in Filmmaking Program.

#ESLSCAUniversity #GettingYouFutureReady

A new chapter in cinematic education is unfolding!

ESLSCA University hosted “Reframing the Scene” during the 9th edition of El Gouna Film Festival, marking the official launch of its MFA in Filmmaking Program.

The event brought together prominent figures, including Eng. Sameh Sawiris, Egyptian Businessman and Founder of El Gouna; Amr Mansi, Executive Director and Co-Founder of El Gouna Film Festival; Yousra, acclaimed Egyptian Actress; Mona El Shazly, renowned TV Presenter and Journalist; and Hussein Fahmy, acclaimed Actor, among other distinguished guests.

Among those representing ESLSCA University were Dr. Kareem ElHennawi, Secretary General & CEO; Dr. Hassan El Meligui, Chief Operating Officer; Mariam Kazmani, Chief of Staff; Dr. Mervat Abou Oaf, Dean of the School of Visual Arts & Creative Industries; Dr. Mohamed Essawy, Senior Director of Institutional Advancement & Undergraduate Programs; Ms. Reem El Meligui, Associate Chair of the Cinematic Studies Department; Dr. Wael Khairy, Director of the MFA in Filmmaking Program; and George Bartlett, Cinematic Studies Academic Instructor.

A milestone in shaping the future of filmmaking education in Egypt!

#ESLSCAUniversity #GettingYouFutureReady

With his leadership in the real estate development sector, Dr. Ahmed Shalaby brings valuable perspectives on business growth, innovation, strategic leadership, and shaping the future of urban development.

Join us for insightful discussions and meaningful conversations with leaders who are driving transformation across industries.

✨ Finally, my V Cola booth design is complete!

Inspired by Ancient Egyptian heritage and the Grand Egyptian Museum, I designed a 3×3 m booth that blends cultural identity with a modern experience.

The concept is inspired by pyramid forms and the colors of Tutankhamun’s mask. It includes a tasting area, a photo corner, a digital screen, and a product display, with animated lighting and AI-generated motion scenes to bring the experience to life.

Designed by: DK designs 🤎✨
